albumBackground:
Johann Sebastian Bach's Mass in B minor (BWV 232) stands as one of the supreme achievements in Western classical music. Karl Richter's seminal 1961 recording with the Münchener Bach-Chor and Münchener Bach-Orchester for Deutsche Grammophon/Archiv Produktion remains a landmark milestone of twentieth-century Baroque performance. Recorded in the acoustic setting of the Musikhochschule in Munich under producer Karl-Heinz Schneider and audio engineer Walter Alfred Wettler, this recording captures Richter's iconic balance of grand architectural rigor, fervent spiritual conviction, and crisp contrapuntal articulation. Featuring a stellar soloist roster including soprano Maria Stader, contralto Hertha Töpper, tenor Ernst Haefliger, and bass Dietrich Fischer-Dieskau, this highlights album ('Chöre und Arien') distills the monumental mass into a single LP vinyl program.

The technical execution of this session relied on early stereo analog recording techniques, employing high-grade Telefunken and Neumann vacuum-tube condenser microphones routed through custom Siemens tube mixing consoles onto two-track analog master tapes. Nippon Polydor's Japanese pressing for Deutsche Grammophon under catalog number MGX7096 benefits from Japan's legendary vinyl manufacturing standards of the 1970s. Pressed on high-purity virgin vinyl with exceptionally quiet surfaces, this Japanese edition provides broad dynamic contrast, wide channel separation, and clear high-frequency fidelity—from subterranean organ pedals to the soaring solo trumpet passages.

For vinyl enthusiasts, this Japanese single-disc pressing offers a focused listening experience that highlights the majestic choral entries and delicate vocal-instrumental duets without needing to navigate the full multi-LP box set. Richter's interpretation, preceding the modern period-instrument movement, strikes a compelling balance between Baroque polyphonic clarity and expressive symphonic weight. Japanese DG pressings from this era are renowned among collectors for their silent noise floor, revealing subtle acoustic reverberation within the hall and precise spatial placement across the stereo field.

tracklist.title: Kyrie eleison I (Chorus)
tracklist.whatToListenFor: Listen for the monumental five-part choral entrance where each vocal line enters with definition against the warm organ pedal and cello continuo depth.

tracklist.title: Gloria in excelsis Deo / Et in terra pax (Chorus)
tracklist.whatToListenFor: Pay attention to the rapid brass fanfare and the seamless transition into the serene, delicate polyphony of 'Et in terra pax'.

tracklist.title: Credo in unum Deum / Patrem omnipotentem (Chorus)
Et incarnatus est (Chorus)
tracklist.whatToListenFor: Hear the hushed string accompaniment and delicate choral vibrato set against the silent Japanese vinyl background.

tracklist.title: Crucifixus (Chorus)
tracklist.whatToListenFor: Notice the chromatic descending passacaglia bass line and the stark dynamic shading as the choir dies down into near stillness.

tracklist.title: Et resurrexit (Chorus)
tracklist.whatToListenFor: Feel the explosive dynamic leap of the full orchestral burst, complete with high-register trumpet flourishes and crisp timpani hits.

tracklist.title: Sanctus (Chorus)
tracklist.whatToListenFor: Focus on the rolling triplet rhythm in the low strings and the wide stereo separation of the six-part choir.

tracklist.title: Dona nobis pacem (Chorus)
tracklist.whatToListenFor: Listen for the triumphant culmination of the entire work where brass, choir, and organ fuse together in full sonic harmony.

vinylTip: This Japanese Nippon Polydor pressing (MGX7096) utilizes silent virgin vinyl. Ensure cartridge overhang and anti-skate are accurately aligned to track the intense inner-groove trumpet high frequencies and dense choral fortissimos on the final tracks of Side B without distortion.
recommendedMood: A meditative Sunday morning or reflective late-evening listening session in a dimly lit room with headphones or high-end stereo speakers.
